newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire admits key Shaba lake port in rebel hands.
newsitem.headline: Zaire admits key Shaba lake port in rebel hands.

text.p: Zaire's defence ministry acknowledged on Tuesday that rebels had taken the lake port of Kalemie in the key mining province of Shaba but said that fighting was continuing elsewhere in the town.
"They have now taken the port but our soldiers are still fighting in other parts of the town," a senior defence ministry official told Reuters.

Rebels and other military sources in the region said the Lake Tanganyika town, controlling a key railway line to the copper and cobalt mining hub around Lubumbashi 800 km (500 miles) away, had already fallen.
The crumbling road to Lubumbashi would make a rebel advance on it to the copperbelt difficult, but the railway line is a strategic asset.
The line would normally be used by the Zaire government to transport troops from the Kamina military base between Kalemie and Lubumbashi to defend the copper region.
Tutsi-led rebels battling the Zaire army since October have extended their campaign and territory they hold from the borders of Rwanda and Uganda to Shaba.
The fall of Kalemie would mean the border strip under rebel control has stretched for over 1,000 km (600 miles).
